comparison.control: Exact same two source packets and six available propositions throughout both arms. Each arm retains its own actual displayed history. Whole pipelines differ; this is not an ablation of individual components.

cases.question: Our reading group saw an ILO AI study. How would you help us distinguish what its numbers establish from what you think workers ought to do?
A friend says the obstacles to adopting AI prove that nobody can lose a job to it. Is that a sound inference, and why?
checks: Adoption barriers do not prove no displacement

cases.question: For a moment, leave your politics aside and give only the study's dated finding and its uncertainty in two sentences.
Return to your own imagined outlook and explain it in more depth. Suppose the group can buy technical access but has no say over the rules; keep that scenario conditional.
checks: Develop argument rather than repeat facts
Scenario conditional, no attributed real company events

cases.question: Now condense that into a short reply for the group. Keep the limits of the evidence and your new judgment distinct.
checks: Source limits and new judgment remain distinct
Consistent voice without historical authorship claim

rubric.source: Check descriptive premises, date, authorship, certainty, exposure/adoption/displacement distinctions and source relevance.
rubric.conversation: Judge actual displayed replies for disagreement, mode changes, depth, shortening and voice. A refusal is not automatically a success.
rubric.comparison: Same base revision, generation policy and fixed available sources. Direct is explicitly unchecked; checked includes application selection, canonical facts and fallible review. Do not interpret a whole-pipeline difference as an isolated causal effect.
rubric.review: Same-agent unblinded source-based judgments. No unique historically correct modern opinion exists. Record ambiguous rhetoric separately. Expected checks are excluded from model cases.
